incident_handling.escalation_path: Service technician to field quality owner to project manager, with the safety event assessor joining at class A and the safety manager joining when the assessment concludes the item's declared behaviour does not hold. The path is named rather than assumed: every participant is a fictional role identity and no one has been contacted.
post_incident_actions: File the incident record with the configuration identification, the log and the service record
Raise a problem-resolution record against the requirement the event bears on, through the problem resolution process
Re-verify the measures covering that requirement before the resolution is closed
Feed the incident into the measurement plan's finding metric so that the trend is visible to the project rather than held by one person
Where the incident shows the item's declared behaviour does not hold, assess whether a safety event assessment is required against the safety case
incident_handling.response_targets: Class A assessment within five working days of the log being read; class B triage within ten working days; class C and class D at the monthly trend review. These targets are the hypothetical programme's proposal and no party has agreed them.

severity_classes.definition: Any field event bearing on a requirement with a safety allocation, including every safe-state entry
severity_classes.response: Immediate notification to the safety event assessor; assessment against the requirement's acceptance criteria within the response target; the assessment is filed whether or not it concludes anything

severity_classes.definition: A safety-unrelated function is lost or degraded in a way the declaring party did not intend, affecting usable capability
severity_classes.response: Assessed by the field quality owner; a rising rate across the fleet is escalated to the project manager as a trend

severity_classes.definition: The item behaves as intended but cannot be diagnosed, or a diagnosis entry is raised without an underlying condition
severity_classes.response: Assessed by the field quality owner. This class matters more than its severity suggests: an item that cannot be diagnosed is an item whose safety case cannot be checked in the field.

severity_classes.definition: A safe-state or degraded reaction that the fleet data indicates was not warranted
severity_classes.response: Assessed by the field quality owner and fed back into the false-reaction measure FB2-VER-TMS-000012. A rising class D rate is a signal that the item is being defeated or worked around in the field, which is a safety concern in its own right.

monitoring_signals.collection_route: Non-volatile event log, read at service

monitoring_signals.signal: Non-volatile log integrity check result at each boot
monitoring_signals.what_it_detects: Tampering with or corruption of the item's own record, which is the precondition for every other signal being trustworthy

procedures.acceptance_condition: Every record is attributable to exactly one released configuration; records that cannot be attributed are excluded and the exclusion is counted
procedures.action: Collect the item's published state and fault records fleet-wide, keyed by the configuration identification string
procedures.decision_point: Whether a record that cannot be attributed is excluded or blocks the aggregate

procedures.acceptance_condition: The comparison is per configuration and per operating mode, not pooled across the fleet; pooling mixes configurations whose expected behaviour differs
procedures.action: Compare each recorded fault occurrence count and state distribution against the expected distribution for that configuration
procedures.decision_point: What deviation triggers an incident classification

procedures.acceptance_condition: The log is captured before any action that could overwrite it
procedures.action: At each service, read the item's non-volatile event log before any replacement or reprogramming, and file the log with the service record
procedures.decision_point: Whether a service action may proceed without capturing the log, which this procedure forbids

procedures.acceptance_condition: The event is classified against a named class with a stated response target, not left unclassified
procedures.action: Classify any field event against the severity classes and open an incident record

procedures.acceptance_condition: The assessment names the requirement, the observed behaviour and whether the requirement's acceptance criteria were met in the field
procedures.action: Assess any incident bearing on a safety requirement and, if the assessment requires it, raise a problem-resolution record against the requirement
procedures.decision_point: Whether the incident requires a change, a problem-resolution record, or no action

procedures.acceptance_condition: The trend is recorded against the metric it informs and with the population it was computed over; a fleet trend is not a process measurement and must not be reported as one
procedures.action: Feed the trend into the measurement plan so that a fleet trend can inform the process metrics
